content.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1665
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1665
- **Title**: gh-1644 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1644` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +468
- **Deletions**: -60
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T08:03:06Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T08:44:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
+#
+# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
+# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
+# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
+# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
+# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
+# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
+# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
+#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
+#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
+#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
+#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
+#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
+#     step for an hour;
+#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
+#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
+#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
+#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
+#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
+#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
+#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
+#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
+#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
+#     only recreations become blobless;
+#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
+#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
+#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
+# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
+set -euo pipefail
+
+url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+
+fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"
+
+# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
+# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
+# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
+# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
+STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)
+
+is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }
+
+recreate_mirror() {
+  local attempt
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
+    rm -rf "$mirror"
+    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
+      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
+  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
+  return 1
+}
+
+if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
+    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
+      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
+      exit 0
+    fi
+    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
+fi
+
+recreate_mirror

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
+# ║  gh-1644 — update_git_mirror.sh self-test                                  ║
+# ║  The contract closes the run-38855793382 incident ("Update local git      ║
+# ║  mirrors" died exit 128 — "error: 2931 bytes of body are still            ║
+# ║  expected"): the old inline workflow logic fetched ONCE (stderr            ║
+# ║  swallowed), fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h       ║
+# ║  transfer died mid-flight, and had no retry and no partial-dir cleanup.   ║
+# ║  Scenarios (local file:// fixture remotes, fault-injected `git` shim):    ║
+# ║    T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror                                ║
+# ║    T2 fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits                     ║
+# ║    T3 a poisoned partial mirror dir is recovered (recreate)               ║
+# ║    T4 THE INCIDENT: transient fetch failure + armed clone failure —       ║
+# ║        a fetch RETRY must recover with NO recreate (the legacy logic      ║
+# ║        recreated, hit the failing clone and died exit 128)                ║
+# ║    T5 persistent clone failure → nonzero exit after exactly               ║
+# ║        MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS logged attempts, ::error marker, no          ║
+# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
+# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
+# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║
+# ║    T7 fetch-retry exhaustion falls back to a successful recreate          ║
+# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
+#
+# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
+# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy
+#   --legacy runs the incident scenarios against the PRE-FIX inline
+#   workflow logic (embedded below, verbatim behavior of the old
+#   build-macos.yml step): every scenario PASSES iff the legacy logic
+#   FAILS the contract — i.e. the bug is reproduced. Zero legacy failures
+#   means the repro is broken.
+
+cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # repo root, any cwd
+MODE="${1:-}"
+SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
+if [ "$MODE" != "--legacy" ] && [ ! -f "$SCRIPT" ]; then
+  echo "❌ $SCRIPT missing — run this selftest from the repo root" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper. This runner prepends a
+# git-push-guard shim to PATH; exec-ing it from OUR shim would ping-pong
+# (the wrapper re-resolves `git` via PATH back into the shim) and spin.
+# `command -v -p` resolves against the system default PATH.
+REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
+if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi
+
+pass=0
+fail=0
+ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
+bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
+label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }
+
+# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
+legacy_update_mirror() {
+  local url="$1" mirror="$2"
+  if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
+    git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
+  else
+    if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
+      echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
+      rm -rf "$mirror"
+      git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
+    fi
+  fi
+}
+
+update_mirror() {
+  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
+    legacy_update_mirror "$@"
+  else
+    bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"
+  fi
+}
+
+# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
+# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
+make_shim() {
+  local dir="$1" fail_fetch="$2" fail_clone="$3"
+  mkdir -p "$dir"
+  echo "$fail_fetch" > "$dir/fetch_left"
+  echo "$fail_clone" > "$dir/clone_left"
+  cat > "$dir/git" <<SHIM
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+REAL_GIT="$REAL_GIT"
+LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
+sub=""; skip=0
+for a in "\$@"; do
+  if [ "\$skip" = 1 ]; then skip=0; continue; fi
+  case "\$a" in
+    -c|-C) skip=1 ;;
+    -*) ;;
+    *) sub="\$a"; break ;;
+  esac
+done
+case "\$sub" in
+  fetch)
+    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
+      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/fetch_left"
+      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
+      echo "fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet" >&2
+      exit 128
+    fi ;;
+  clone)
+    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
+      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/clone_left"
+      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
+      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2
+      exit 128
+    fi ;;
+esac
+exec "\$REAL_GIT" "\$@"
+SHIM
+  chmod +x "$dir/git"
+}
+
+use_shim() {  # $1 = shim dir ("" = restore real git)
+  if [ -n "$1" ]; then PATH="$1:$REAL_PATH"; else PATH="$REAL_PATH"; fi
+}
+
+# ── fixture: a local bare "origin" ──────────────────────────────────────────
+make_fixture() {
+  local d="$1"
+  git init -q "$d/work"
+  git -C "$d/work" config user.email t@example.com
+  git -C "$d/work" config user.name t
+  echo one > "$d/work/file.txt"
+  git -C "$d/work" add .
+  git -C "$d/work" commit -qm one
+  git clone -q --bare "$d/work" "$d/remote.git"
+}
+
+advance_fixture() {  # $1 = fixture root — one more commit on the remote
+  git -C "$1/work" commit -qm "two-$RANDOM" --allow-empty
+  git -C "$1/work" push -q "$1/remote.git" HEAD
+}
+
+mirror_head() { git -C "$1" log --oneline -1 2>/dev/null | head -1; }
+
+export REAL_PATH="$PATH"
+export MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP=0
+
+# ══ T1: fresh clone creates a working mirror ════════════════════════════════
+t1() {
+  local d="$WORK/t1"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
+  local out rc
+  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
+  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
+    ok "T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror ($(label_legacy))"
+  else
+    bad "T1 fresh clone FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
+  fi
+}
+
+# ══ T2: fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits ═════════════════════
+t2() {
+  local d="$WORK/t2"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
+  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local before after
+  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
+  advance_fixture "$d"
+  local out rc
+  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
+  after=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
+  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$before" != "$after" ]; then
+    ok "T2 fetch advances the mirror ($(label_legacy))"
+  else
+    bad "T2 fetch update FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc before='$before' after='$after' — $out"
+  fi
+}
+
+# ══ T3: poisoned partial dir is recovered ═══════════════════════════════════
+t3() {
+  local d="$WORK/t3"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
+  mkdir -p "$d/mirror.git"          # partial dir left by a killed clone
+  echo garbage > "$d/mirror.git/HEAD"
+  local out rc
+  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
+  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
+    ok "T3 poisoned partial dir recovered ($(label_legacy))"
+  else
+    bad "T3 poisoned-dir recovery FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
+  fi
+}
+
+# ══ T4: THE INCIDENT — transient fetch failure, clone armed to fail ═════════
+# The old logic must NOT pass here: it swallowed the fetch error, recreated
+# and died on the failing clone (run 38855793382, exit 128). The fixed
+# script must recover via a fetch RETRY with NO recreate at all.
+t4() {
+  local d="$WORK/t4"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
+  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local before

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
+#
+# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
+# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
+# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
+# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
+# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
+# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
+# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
+#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
+#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
+#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
+#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
+#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
+#     step for an hour;
+#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
+#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
+#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
+#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
+#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
+#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
+#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
+#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
+#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
+#     only recreations become blobless;
+#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
+#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
+#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
+# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
+set -euo pipefail
+
+url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+
+fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"
+
+# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
+# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
+# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
+# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
+STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)
+
+is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }
+
+recreate_mirror() {
+  local attempt
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
+    rm -rf "$mirror"
+    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
+      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
+  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
+  return 1
+}
+
+if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
+    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
+      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
+      exit 0
+    fi
+    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
+fi
+
+recreate_mirror

+# ║  gh-1644 — update_git_mirror.sh self-test                                  ║
+# ║  The contract closes the run-38855793382 incident ("Update local git      ║
+# ║  mirrors" died exit 128 — "error: 2931 bytes of body are still            ║

+# ║  Scenarios (local file:// fixture remotes, fault-injected `git` shim):    ║

+# ║    T2 fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits                     ║
+# ║    T3 a poisoned partial mirror dir is recovered (recreate)               ║

+# ║        a fetch RETRY must recover with NO recreate (the legacy logic      ║
+# ║        recreated, hit the failing clone and died exit 128)                ║
+# ║    T5 persistent clone failure → nonzero exit after exactly               ║
+# ║        MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS logged attempts, ::error marker, no          ║
+# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
+# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
+# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║
+# ║    T7 fetch-retry exhaustion falls back to a successful recreate          ║
+# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
+#
+# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
+# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy
+#   --legacy runs the incident scenarios against the PRE-FIX inline
+#   workflow logic (embedded below, verbatim behavior of the old
+#   build-macos.yml step): every scenario PASSES iff the legacy logic
+#   FAILS the contract — i.e. the bug is reproduced. Zero legacy failures
+#   means the repro is broken.
+
+cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # repo root, any cwd
+MODE="${1:-}"
+SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
+if [ "$MODE" != "--legacy" ] && [ ! -f "$SCRIPT" ]; then
+  echo "❌ $SCRIPT missing — run this selftest from the repo root" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper. This runner prepends a
+# git-push-guard shim to PATH; exec-ing it from OUR shim would ping-pong
+# (the wrapper re-resolves `git` via PATH back into the shim) and spin.
+# `command -v -p` resolves against the system default PATH.

+if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi
+
+pass=0
+fail=0
+ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
+bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
+label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }
+
+# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
+legacy_update_mirror() {
+  local url="$1" mirror="$2"
+  if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
+    git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
+  else
+    if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
+      echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
+      rm -rf "$mirror"
+      git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"

+  fi

+update_mirror() {
+  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
+    legacy_update_mirror "$@"
+  else
+    bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"
+  fi

+# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
+# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
+make_shim() {
+  local dir="$1" fail_fetch="$2" fail_clone="$3"
+  mkdir -p "$dir"
+  echo "$fail_fetch" > "$dir/fetch_left"
+  echo "$fail_clone" > "$dir/clone_left"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+REAL_GIT="$REAL_GIT"
+LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
+sub=""; skip=0
+for a in "\$@"; do
+  if [ "\$skip" = 1 ]; then skip=0; continue; fi
+  case "\$a" in
+    -c|-C) skip=1 ;;
+    -*) ;;
+    *) sub="\$a"; break ;;
+  esac
+done
+case "\$sub" in
+  fetch)
+    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
+      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/fetch_left"
+      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
+      echo "fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet" >&2
+      exit 128
+    fi ;;
+  clone)
+    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
+      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/clone_left"
+      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
+      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2
+      exit 128
+    fi ;;
+esac
+exec "\$REAL_GIT" "\$@"
+SHIM
+  chmod +x "$dir/git"
+}
+
+use_shim() {  # $1 = shim dir ("" = restore real git)
+  if [ -n "$1" ]; then PATH="$1:$REAL_PATH"; else PATH="$REAL_PATH"; fi
+}
+
+# ── fixture: a local bare "origin" ──────────────────────────────────────────
+make_fixture() {
+  local d="$1"
+  git init -q "$d/work"
+  git -C "$d/work" config user.email t@example.com
+  git -C "$d/work" config user.name t
+  echo one > "$d/work/file.txt"
+  git -C "$d/work" add .
+  git -C "$d/work" commit -qm one
+  git clone -q --bare "$d/work" "$d/remote.git"
+}
+
+advance_fixture() {  # $1 = fixture root — one more commit on the remote
+  git -C "$1/work" commit -qm "two-$RANDOM" --allow-empty
+  git -C "$1/work" push -q "$1/remote.git" HEAD
+}
+
+mirror_head() { git -C "$1" log --oneline -1 2>/dev/null | head -1; }
+
+export REAL_PATH="$PATH"
+export MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP=0
+
+# ══ T1: fresh clone creates a working mirror ════════════════════════════════
+t1() {
+  local d="$WORK/t1"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
+  local out rc
+  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
+  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
+    ok "T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror ($(label_legacy))"
+  else
+    bad "T1 fresh clone FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
+  fi
+}
+
+# ══ T2: fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits ═════════════════════
+t2() {
+  local d="$WORK/t2"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"

+  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")

+  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
+  after=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
+  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$before" != "$after" ]; then
+    ok "T2 fetch advances the mirror ($(label_legacy))"
+  else
+    bad "T2 fetch update FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc before='$before' after='$after' — $out"
+  fi
+}
+
+# ══ T3: poisoned partial dir is recovered ═══════════════════════════════════
+t3() {
+  local d="$WORK/t3"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"

+  echo garbage > "$d/mirror.git/HEAD"

+  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
+#
+# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
+# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
+# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
+# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
+# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
+# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
+# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
+#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
+#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
+#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
+#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
+#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
+#     step for an hour;
+#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
+#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
+#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
+#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
+#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
+#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
+#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
+#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
+#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
+#     only recreations become blobless;
+#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
+#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
+#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
+# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
+set -euo pipefail
+
+url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+
+fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"
+
+# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
+# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
+# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
+# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
+STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

+  local attempt
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
+    rm -rf "$mirror"
+    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
+      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
+  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
+  return 1
+}
+
+if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
+    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
+      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
+      exit 0
+    fi
+    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
+fi
+
+recreate_mirror

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1665
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1665
- **Title**: gh-1644 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1644` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +468
- **Deletions**: -60
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T08:03:06Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T08:44:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
+#
+# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
+# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
+# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
+# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
+# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
+# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
+# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
+#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
+#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
+#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
+#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
+#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
+#     step for an hour;
+#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
+#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
+#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
+#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
+#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
+#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
+#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
+#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
+#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
+#     only recreations become blobless;
+#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
+#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
+#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
+#
+# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
+# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
+set -euo pipefail
+
+url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
+
+fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"
+
+# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
+# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
+# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
+# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
+STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)
+
+is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }
+
+recreate_mirror() {
+  local attempt
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
+    rm -rf "$mirror"
+    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
+      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
+  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
+  return 1
+}
+
+if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
+  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
+    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
+    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
+      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
+      exit 0
+    fi
+    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
+    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
+      sleep "$retry_sleep"
+    fi
+  done
+  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
+fi
+
+recreate_mirror

+# ║  Scenarios (local file:// fixture remotes, fault-injected `git` shim):    ║

+# ║    T2 fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits                     ║

+# ║        MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS logged attempts, ::error marker, no          ║
+# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
+# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
+# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).
