# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

But a subtle issue: `--reference` without `--shared` copies... actually `--reference` sets up alternates; with `--depth=1` git fetches the tip commit + blobs from origin. Blobless mirror has commits/trees, so the fetch pack will be small. Fine, and gh-1477 precedent exists per PR description. Let me verify gh-1477 precedent actually exists — grep for it.

**2. Potential issue: `git clone --reference` with a blobless mirror and `git gc`/maintenance on the checkout repo could try to follow alternates into missing objects.** Minor, no auto-gc in CI typically. Not worth flagging strongly.

**3. Stall guard on fetch**: `git -C "$mirror" fetch origin` with `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60`. For an up-to-date mirror, fetch transfers little; lowSpeedLimit applies when data is flowing; if 0 bytes for 60s it aborts. A quiet connection during the initial negotiation could false-positive? lowSpeedTime triggers only when transfer is below limit cumulatively over the window... Actually git's low speed check: aborts if transfer speed is below lowSpeedLimit for lowSpeedTime seconds. During protocol v2 negotiation silence, git resets the timer on activity. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
  rm -rf "$mirror"
  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
  return 0
fi
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Not blocking — with blobless clones the recreate window is minutes, and the partial-dir cleanup contract (T5) is preserved either way.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name

        id: version
        run: |

            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")

              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
  rm -rf "$mirror"
  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
  return 0
fi
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Not blocking — with blobless clones the recreate window is minutes, and the partial-dir cleanup contract (T5) is preserved either way.

## Review summary

**What the PR does well:** The new `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` is well-documented and genuinely resilient — fetch retries with visible stderr, a stall abort guard, blobless (`--filter=blob:none`, gh-1477 precedent) recreates with retries and partial-dir cleanup, and a selftest with a legacy replay mode that reproduces the incident. I verified locally: selftest 7/7 PASS, legacy mode 4/4 repro, `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS, YAML parses, `bash -n` clean, both scripts executable. The size-budget reseed uses the established `<rev>` normalization and the gate's documented escape hatch. The dead `extra_args` branch of the old inline function had no remaining callers, so nothing was lost.

**Blocking finding (new failure mode introduced by the fix):** All 3 converted steps (`build-macos.yml:125`, `build-mobile.yml:625` build-ios, `build-mobile.yml:1059` submit-ios) invoke `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` as the **first step of their jobs, before any checkout**. On these persistent self-hosted runners the workspace holds the previous run's clone (proven by the checkout steps doing `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`), so the first run after merge executes with a **pre-merge workspace that lacks the script** → exit 127 → all four affected legs go red once and gh-1644 (auto-closes only on green) stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency. Fix: bootstrap the script from the freshly-updated mirror (`git --git-dir=$MIRROR show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`) or fetch it pinned to `${{ github.sha }}`.

**Suggestion:** `recreate_mirror` deletes the last good mirror before cloning — recreate into a temp dir and swap on success so a failed recreate doesn't leave zero mirrors.

Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. - `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

**1. `--reference` clone against a blobless mirror.** The checkout steps use `git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 https://...`. With a blob:none mirror, when the depth-1 clone needs tip blobs, it downloads them from origin — works. But a subtle issue: `--reference` without `--shared` copies... actually `--reference` sets up alternates; with `--depth=1` git fetches the tip commit + blobs from origin. Blobless mirror has commits/trees, so the fetch pack will be small. Fine, and gh-1477 precedent exists per PR description. Let me verify gh-1477 precedent actually exists — grep for it.

**2. Potential issue: `git clone --reference` with a blobless mirror and `git gc`/maintenance on the checkout repo could try to follow alternates into missing objects.** Minor, no auto-gc in CI typically. Not worth flagging strongly.

**3. Stall guard on fetch**: `git -C "$mirror" fetch origin` with `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60`. For an up-to-date mirror, fetch transfers little; lowSpeedLimit applies when data is flowing; if 0 bytes for 60s it aborts. A quiet connection during the initial negotiation could false-positive? lowSpeedTime triggers only when transfer is below limit cumulatively over the window... Actually git's low speed check: aborts if transfer speed is below lowSpeedLimit for lowSpeedTime seconds. During protocol v2 negotiation silence, git resets the timer on activity. Known caveat but acceptable; it matches the incident (62-min transfer).

**4. Security/workflow review**: The workflow changes don't touch permissions or secrets. The script takes url/mirror as args — invoked only with hardcoded values. No injection vector. `rm -rf "$mirror"` — mirror path is controlled. Fine.

Is that a regression? If the mirror is deleted and clone fails, next run recreates. But dependent checkout would fail anyway if network is down. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
  rm -rf "$mirror"
  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
  return 0
fi
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Not blocking — with blobless clones the recreate window is minutes, and the partial-dir cleanup contract (T5) is preserved either way.

On a FRESH runner (no mirror yet — e.g., first ever run or wiped mirror dir), the mirror doesn't exist → fallback fails → `::error::` exit 1. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Now the deeper review analysis. Points to consider:

**1. `--reference` clone against a blobless mirror.** The checkout steps use `git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 https://...`. With a blob:none mirror, when the depth-1 clone needs tip blobs, it downloads them from origin — works. But a subtle issue: `--reference` without `--shared` copies... actually `--reference` sets up alternates; with `--depth=1` git fetches the tip commit + blobs from origin. Blobless mirror has commits/trees, so the fetch pack will be small. Fine, and gh-1477 precedent exists per PR description. Let me verify gh-1477 precedent actually exists — grep for it.

**2. Potential issue: `git clone --reference` with a blobless mirror and `git gc`/maintenance on the checkout repo could try to follow alternates into missing objects.** Minor, no auto-gc in CI typically. Not worth flagging strongly.

**3. Stall guard on fetch**: `git -C "$mirror" fetch origin` with `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60`. For an up-to-date mirror, fetch transfers little; lowSpeedLimit applies when data is flowing; if 0 bytes for 60s it aborts. A quiet connection during the initial negotiation could false-positive? lowSpeedTime triggers only when transfer is below limit cumulatively over the window... Actually git's low speed check: aborts if transfer speed is below lowSpeedLimit for lowSpeedTime seconds. During protocol v2 negotiation silence, git resets the timer on activity. Known caveat but acceptable; it matches the incident (62-min transfer).

**4. Security/workflow review**: The workflow changes don't touch permissions or secrets. The script takes url/mirror as args — invoked only with hardcoded values. No injection vector. `rm -rf "$mirror"` — mirror path is controlled. Fine.

**5. `fetch` retries then falls back to recreate which does `rm -rf "$mirror"`** — one edge: if the remote is persistently down, the script deletes a good (but stale) mirror after fetch attempts fail and clone fails — ends with NO mirror at all, whereas before it left the stale mirror. Is that a regression? If the mirror is deleted and clone fails, next run recreates. But dependent checkout would fail anyway if network is down. Trade-off: keeping a stale mirror would let checkout proceed offline... Actually checkout needs `--depth=1` fetch from origin anyway, so it needs network regardless. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
  rm -rf "$mirror"
  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
  return 0
fi
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Not blocking — with blobless clones the recreate window is minutes, and the partial-dir cleanup contract (T5) is preserved either way.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Now the deeper review analysis. Points to consider:

**1. `--reference` clone against a blobless mirror.** The checkout steps use `git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 https://...`. With a blob:none mirror, when the depth-1 clone needs tip blobs, it downloads them from origin — works. But a subtle issue: `--reference` without `--shared` copies... actually `--reference` sets up alternates; with `--depth=1` git fetches the tip commit + blobs from origin. Blobless mirror has commits/trees, so the fetch pack will be small. Fine, and gh-1477 precedent exists per PR description. Let me verify gh-1477 precedent actually exists — grep for it.

**2. Potential issue: `git clone --reference` with a blobless mirror and `git gc`/maintenance on the checkout repo could try to follow alternates into missing objects.** Minor, no auto-gc in CI typically. Not worth flagging strongly.

**3. Stall guard on fetch**: `git -C "$mirror" fetch origin` with `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60`. For an up-to-date mirror, fetch transfers little; lowSpeedLimit applies when data is flowing; if 0 bytes for 60s it aborts. A quiet connection during the initial negotiation could false-positive? lowSpeedTime triggers only when transfer is below limit cumulatively over the window... Actually git's low speed check: aborts if transfer speed is below lowSpeedLimit for lowSpeedTime seconds. During protocol v2 negotiation silence, git resets the timer on activity. Known caveat but acceptable; it matches the incident (62-min transfer).

**4. Security/workflow review**: The workflow changes don't touch permissions or secrets. The script takes url/mirror as args — invoked only with hardcoded values. No injection vector. `rm -rf "$mirror"` — mirror path is controlled. Fine.

**5. `fetch` retries then falls back to recreate which does `rm -rf "$mirror"`** — one edge: if the remote is persistently down, the script deletes a good (but stale) mirror after fetch attempts fail and clone fails — ends with NO mirror at all, whereas before it left the stale mirror. Is that a regression? If the mirror is deleted and clone fails, next run recreates. But dependent checkout would fail anyway if network is down. Trade-off: keeping a stale mirror would let checkout proceed offline... Actually checkout needs `--depth=1` fetch from origin anyway, so it needs network regardless. Deleting is consistent with "no partial dir". Acceptable; maybe a SUGGESTION.

**6. TSV reseed**: TOTAL went 78579365 → 73347265 (smaller). Size decreased mainly due to canvaskit rev dir normalization? No — the old rows had concrete rev dir `deb287...` with same sizes; normalization collapses path only. The decrease: removed skills assets (-70386 SKILL.md and other skills rows?), main.dart.js grew 11582554→12116395 (+4.6%? that's +4.9%... PR says +4.6%). Hmm 12116395/11582554 = 1.0461 → +4.6%. OK. agent.js 1791532→1887086 = +5.33%.

Wait — but the ticket says the gate failed with agent.js at +5.3% vs +5.0% budget. The reseed makes agent.js the new floor at 1887086. Fine — that's the documented escape hatch.

One concern: the removed `panel/app/assets/skills/` rows — PR notes "−removed skills assets". OK documented.

**7. Consistency check: does the workflow gate command use this TSV?** Check build workflow for size gate invocation to make sure TSV format matches (with <rev> placeholders supported via normalization on load — confirmed by selftest "literal-rev baseline migrates on load").

**8. Selftest T4 check**: `mirror_head` equals before — fetch retry recovers; good.

**9. One real issue candidate**: In `recreate_mirror`, `git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` — when recreating a mirror that was previously FULL and used by OTHER consumers... only these workflows use it, all with --depth=1 checkouts. Fine.

**10. Legacy mode in selftest**: `t4` legacy: `make_shim "$d/shim" 1 1` — fetch fails once, clone would fail once. legacy: fetch fails → recreate → clone fails (armed 1) → dies 128. Confirmed.

**11. `--mirror` + `--filter=blob:none` on GitHub**: works, server supports filter (gh-1477 precedent). For the fixture (file://), filter is a no-op but config still recorded — T6 verified.

**12. Potential issue: `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` into `$mirror` — if `$mirror` parent doesn't exist? In workflows they `mkdir -p` the base first. In recreate, `rm -rf "$mirror"` then clone creates it. git clone creates the dir. Fine.

**13. `sleep "$retry_sleep"` between attempts with default 10s; total worst case: 3 fetch attempts + 3 clone attempts with sleeps ≈ under a minute. Fine.

**14. `set -euo pipefail` + `((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++))` arithmetic: with `set -e`, `((attempt++))` at the point where expression evaluates to 0 could exit... Here it's `attempt=$((attempt+1))` style inside for-loop arithmetic `((attempt = 1; ...))` — a for loop's arithmetic command failing with status 1 (when condition false) is fine in a for loop context (not subject to set -e). Confirmed by selftest passing.

**15. ci_failures.md** — not present input/, so no CI blocking data. The ticket shows the dev machine job done ✅. I can't fetch CI status; note absence.

**16. Memory notes added** (n_1001_5ff8, n_1001_90cb) — agent memory notes committed to repo. That's repo convention apparently (memory/ dir exists). Check memory/ dir — yes, `memory/` exists at root. Fine.

**17. One more check**: does anything else in workflows still use the deleted inline pattern or reference `update_git_mirror.sh` from a working directory other than repo root? The workflow steps run at repo root by default (checkout happens AFTER mirror update though!). Wait — critical: the "Update local git mirrors" step runs BEFORE checkout. What is the working directory at that point? GitHub Actions default working-directory is `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, which is the checked-out repo... but these are self-hosted runners that `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` in the checkout step. In the "Update local git mirrors" step, actions/checkout has ALREADY run? Let me look at the workflow order — is there a `actions/checkout` step before "Update local git mirrors"? In build-macos.yml, the checkout-from-mirrors step comes after. But GitHub auto-checkout doesn't happen unless actions/checkout is used. So what is $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at the mirror-update step — does `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` exist there?

Hmm, this is important. If no actions/checkout ran before, the workspace might contain leftovers from a previous run on this persistent runner (they rm -rf it in checkout step, but that runs after). Actually on a persistent self-hosted runner, $GITHUB_WORKSPACE persists between runs! The previous run's checkout step did `rm -rf $GITHUB_WORKSPACE; git clone ... $GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, leaving the repo at the OLD commit. So `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` would exist (from the previous run's checkout) — but at the OLD revision without the new script... on the very first run after merge, the mirror update would run with the previous commit's workspace, which lacks `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` → `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` fails "No such file"!

Wait — but the old inline logic had the same property: no checkout needed before. The new script introduces a dependency on the workspace containing the repo. Is there a checkout step before "Update local git mirrors" in build-macos.yml? Let me check the full job steps. Also check what the old build-mobile.yml did — it also had inline logic, no script dependency. Let me verify whether any actions/checkout precedes.

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
  rm -rf "$mirror"
  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
  return 0
fi
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Not blocking — with blobless clones the recreate window is minutes, and the partial-dir cleanup contract (T5) is preserved either way.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Now the deeper review analysis. Points to consider:

**1. `--reference` clone against a blobless mirror.** The checkout steps use `git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 https://...`. With a blob:none mirror, when the depth-1 clone needs tip blobs, it downloads them from origin — works. But a subtle issue: `--reference` without `--shared` copies... actually `--reference` sets up alternates; with `--depth=1` git fetches the tip commit + blobs from origin. Blobless mirror has commits/trees, so the fetch pack will be small. Fine, and gh-1477 precedent exists per PR description. Let me verify gh-1477 precedent actually exists — grep for it.

**2. Potential issue: `git clone --reference` with a blobless mirror and `git gc`/maintenance on the checkout repo could try to follow alternates into missing objects.** Minor, no auto-gc in CI typically. Not worth flagging strongly.

**3. Stall guard on fetch**: `git -C "$mirror" fetch origin` with `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60`. For an up-to-date mirror, fetch transfers little; lowSpeedLimit applies when data is flowing; if 0 bytes for 60s it aborts. A quiet connection during the initial negotiation could false-positive? lowSpeedTime triggers only when transfer is below limit cumulatively over the window... Actually git's low speed check: aborts if transfer speed is below lowSpeedLimit for lowSpeedTime seconds. During protocol v2 negotiation silence, git resets the timer on activity. Known caveat but acceptable; it matches the incident (62-min transfer).

**4. Security/workflow review**: The workflow changes don't touch permissions or secrets. The script takes url/mirror as args — invoked only with hardcoded values. No injection vector. `rm -rf "$mirror"` — mirror path is controlled. Fine.

**5. `fetch` retries then falls back to recreate which does `rm -rf "$mirror"`** — one edge: if the remote is persistently down, the script deletes a good (but stale) mirror after fetch attempts fail and clone fails — ends with NO mirror at all, whereas before it left the stale mirror. Is that a regression? If the mirror is deleted and clone fails, next run recreates. But dependent checkout would fail anyway if network is down. Trade-off: keeping a stale mirror would let checkout proceed offline... Actually checkout needs `--depth=1` fetch from origin anyway, so it needs network regardless. Deleting is consistent with "no partial dir". Acceptable; maybe a SUGGESTION.

**6. TSV reseed**: TOTAL went 78579365 → 73347265 (smaller). Size decreased mainly due to canvaskit rev dir normalization? No — the old rows had concrete rev dir `deb287...` with same sizes; normalization collapses path only. The decrease: removed skills assets (-70386 SKILL.md and other skills rows?), main.dart.js grew 11582554→12116395 (+4.6%? that's +4.9%... PR says +4.6%). Hmm 12116395/11582554 = 1.0461 → +4.6%. **8. Selftest T4 check**: `mirror_head` equals before — fetch retry recovers; good.

**9. One real issue candidate**: In `recreate_mirror`, `git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` — when recreating a mirror that was previously FULL and used by OTHER consumers... only these workflows use it, all with --depth=1 checkouts. Fine.

            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")

              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
  rm -rf "$mirror"
  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
  return 0
fi
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Not blocking — with blobless clones the recreate window is minutes, and the partial-dir cleanup contract (T5) is preserved either way.

> ℹ️ **3 resolved thread(s) excluded; 2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 4

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The resilience logic itself is solid (7/7 selftest + 4/4 legacy repro verified locally), but all three converted mirror steps call `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` before any checkout — on the persistent self-hosted runners the first post-merge run executes with a pre-merge workspace where the script doesn't exist, so every affected leg fails once with exit 127 and gh-1644 stays open.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `build-macos.yml` / `build-mobile.yml` mirror steps depend on workspace content that cannot exist yet on the first run after merge (bootstrap the script from the mirror or `${{ github.sha }}` instead)
- 💡 `recreate_mirror` deletes the last good mirror before cloning — recreate into a temp dir and swap on success

**Next Steps**:
1. Remove the pre-checkout workspace dependency at all 3 call sites (see inline threads)
2. (Optional) temp-dir swap in `recreate_mirror`
3. Re-run `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` — it passes as-is and needs no change for either fix

# Rework — gh-1644 review threads (PR #1665)

## Issues/Notes

All three findings from the automated review are addressed in code on the rework head (`9cdf47b0`):

- **BLOCKING (build-macos.yml)**: `Update local git mirrors` was the first step of the job with no checkout before it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` read from the persisted workspace — a pre-merge tree on the first post-merge run (exit 127).
- **BLOCKING (build-mobile.yml `build-ios` + `submit-ios`)**: identical first-run failure mode at both mirror steps.
- **SUGGESTION**: `recreate_mirror` deleted the last good mirror before cloning; a fully-failed recreate left no mirror at all.

No CI failures on the rework head (`input/gh-1644/ci_failures.md` — all checks green). No merge conflicts.

## Approach

TDD per finding — each fix was proven by a failing-then-passing test in `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh`:

1. **Bootstrap without workspace dependency (both BLOCKING threads)**: all 3 mirror steps now write the script to `$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh` — fetched via `curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors` from the commit-pinned raw URL (`raw.githubusercontent.com/.../${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`, valid because these are `workflow_dispatch`-only workflows so `github.sha` is always a pushed commit), with `git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"` (branch resolved dynamically via `symbolic-ref`, `main` fallback) as the no-network fallback. Both sources failing exits 1 with a precise `::error::`. New selftest scenario **T9** asserts the mirror-extracted copy is a complete, parseable script that runs standalone (confirmed RED before the fix — extraction previously assumed a hardcoded `main`).
2. **Temp-dir swap in `recreate_mirror` (SUGGESTION)**: the blobless clone now lands in the sibling `"$mirror.recreate"` and is swapped in only on success (`rm -rf "$mirror" && mv`); on exhaustion the temp dir is removed and the last good mirror survives. Header contract comment updated. New selftest scenario **T8** fault-injects every fetch and clone attempt to fail and asserts nonzero exit, `::error::`, unchanged mirror head, and no `.recreate` leftover — confirmed RED against the old delete-first logic.

## Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` — `Update local git mirrors` step bootstraps the script into `$RUNNER_TEMP` (curl pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` + dynamic-branch mirror fallback); no `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` reference before checkout.
- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` — same bootstrap at both `Update local git mirror` steps (`build-ios`, `submit-ios`).
- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` — `recreate_mirror` clones into `"$mirror.recreate"` and swaps on success; last good mirror preserved on total failure.
- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` — new T8 (last-good-mirror preservation) and T9 (mirror-extracted bootstrap) scenarios; headers updated.

## Test Coverage

- `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` → **10/10 PASS** (T1–T9; T9 has two assertions). Run from repo root.
- `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy` → **4/4 PASS** — every legacy pass reproduces the pre-fix incident (exit 128 on the incident shape, single-shot recreate, no blobless filter), confirming the regression net still catches the original bug.
- Functional sandbox test of the verbatim bootstrap run block: curl-down→mirror-fallback ✅, curl-up ✅, both-down→`::error::` + exit 1 ✅ — the workspace is never referenced.
- `bash -n` clean on both shell scripts; `yaml.safe_load` parses both touched workflows; `git diff --check` clean; `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv` reseed intact (TOTAL 73347265); CI checks green on the rework head.

## Review threads

Replies for all 3 open threads are in `outputs/review_replies/` (see `outputs/review_replies.json`): the substantive review summary (thread 4) plus the two machine audit records (threads 5, 7).

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. The step fails with `bash: scripts/update_git_mirror.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) before the resilience logic ever runs. All four affected legs (build-macos arm64/x86_64, build-ios, submit-ios) go red once, and gh-1644 — which auto-closes only when the leg goes green — stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency; the fix introduces one.

(If the runner were instead configured to wipe the workspace, the step fails the same way — only a post-merge workspace makes this line work.)

Suggested fix — bootstrap the script without depending on the checked-out tree, e.g. after a minimal inline "ensure mirror exists + one fetch" prelude (cheap; the script's retries still own the resilience):

```bash
# mirror already ensured + fetched inline above
git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```
